correctness.rationale: The nonparallel axis normals and common orthogonal direction provide an invertible affine map T, determinant |sin beta|; in canonical coordinates the intersection is two quadratic cylinder constraints. The centered inscribed ellipsoid with semiaxes (a,b,b) is certified by the six signed principal-axis contacts and John covariance. For the proposed Löwner form, its squared gauge is a positive linear combination of the two cylinder gauges and saturates on the common ridge. Two signed contact orbits have positive weights p0=(1+u)/3, p1=(2-u)/3, whose normalized covariance is I/3, certifying global minimum volume. The identity t(2u-1)=u(2-u) yields the radical u and strictly increasing ratio 2 to 3sqrt3/2 for a/b>=1. Affine volume cancels beta; the orthogonal case is the p=q=1 edge of record #3.
